clue.text: Shellfish from Yellow Sea exported to France

blocks.note: or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow
the French word for sea

explanation.surface: A seafood importer traces a shellfish caught in Chinese waters and shipped to France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exported to France' asks for the French translation of sea. OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is an edible ear-shaped mollusc found around the Channel Islands, also called abalone.

clue.text: Public holiday causes epidemic

blocks.note: a secret that is out is public knowledge
a short holiday is a break

explanation.surface: A bank holiday crowd spreads a disease around the country.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak is a sudden rise in cases of a disease, which is what an epidemic consists of.

clue.text: Normal clue lacking definition ultimately becomes elementary?

indicators.note: something lacking is missing, so a letter is taken out of the fodder
ultimately points to the final letter of the word it follows
the letters turn into something else, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of definition

explanation.surface: A setter jokes that an ordinary clue without its definition becomes elementary.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: molecules are built from the elements, so at their level things are 'elementary' in a punning sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Molecular describes the smallest particles of a compound, a basic level of matter, so it is playfully 'elementary'.

clue.text: Revolt as a result of undesirable uprising

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: a leper is a social outcast, an undesirable

explanation.surface: A revolt breaks out because some unwelcome group has risen up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolt' looks like a noun but is the verb: to disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt someone is to disgust them, which is one sense of repel, driving them away in distaste.

clue.text: Religious figure asks questions atheists regularly disregarded

indicators.note: every other letter is ignored at a steady interval, keeping only the alternate ones

blocks.note: to pry is to ask nosy questions
second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A cleric fields questions from unbelievers, whose objections are routinely ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A priestess is a woman who performs sacred rites, a female religious official.

clue.text: Established church driven out of French region

indicators.note: something driven out of a place is expelled, so it is removed from the word

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
the region of south-east France

explanation.surface: The established church is expelled from a part of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Established church' reads as one phrase, the Church of England; split it after 'Established'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something proven has been shown true and accepted, so it is established as fact.

clue.text: Showing some reluctance to go initially in latrine that's out of order

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word
a sequence out of order is jumbled, so the letters need rearranging

blocks.note: first letter of in
its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates to use a broken toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reading of 'reluctance to go' is lavatorial; the definition is physics, the tendency of a body to resist starting to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is resistance to a change in motion, so inertial describes a body reluctant to start moving.

clue.text: Sucking noises suppress last couple of kisses

indicators.note: the final pair of letters of the next word are kept

blocks.note: to squelch a rumour is to suppress it
the final two letters

explanation.surface: A couple's final kisses are stifled, leaving only wet sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Squelches are the wet sucking sounds made by feet pulled out of mud.

clue.text: Journalist covering men battling enemy primarily

definitions.text: Journalist covering men battling enemy primarily

indicators.note: one piece covers the other, going around it on both sides
primarily means firstly, so the opening letter of each preceding word is used

blocks.note: ED is short for editor
the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A reporter travels with troops who are fighting the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: an embedded reporter lives with soldiers to cover their battles.
explanation.definitionFit: An embed is a war reporter attached to a military unit, reporting from among the fighting troops.

clue.text: Unruffled by lifting of some hygiene restrictions

indicators.note: some of the letters are wanted, so the answer sits inside the words that follow
in a down entry, lifting reads the letters upwards, from the end back

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: People stay calm as Covid hygiene rules are relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene means calm and untroubled, the state of someone who is not ruffled or agitated.

clue.text: What might one call a huge sum?

blocks.note: first meaning: the digits you dial to ring someone
second meaning: British slang for an enormous figure with very many digits

explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a salary or fee in 'telephone numbers' is one so large it has as many digits as a phone number.
explanation.definitionFit: You call a person on their phone line by dialling it, and the idiom names a sum with many digits.

clue.text: Bring to mind prayer after bible class

blocks.note: RE is religious education, a school subject
a collect is a short prayer in a church service

explanation.surface: A pupil remembers a prayer after Sunday-school lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the prayer behind the class. A collect, stressed on the first syllable, is a short liturgical prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: To recollect is to remember, calling a past event back into memory.

clue.text: Lacking in energy, gloomy and weighed down

indicators.note: lacking something means it is missing, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy
a leaden sky is grey and gloomy

explanation.surface: Someone is listless, depressed and burdened.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means heavily loaded, carrying a burden that presses it down.

clue.text: Firm undergoing cyclical readjustment with supreme competence

indicators.note: a cyclical change rotates the letters, moving some from the front to the back

blocks.note: firm and steady

explanation.surface: A company goes through restructuring with great skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the first two letters of the word for firm to its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablest is the superlative of able, so it describes whoever is most competent of all.

clue.text: Plot contains treasure under layers of rock

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under means placed below, so this piece follows the other

blocks.note: geological layers
a gem is a treasure

explanation.surface: A story features buried treasure beneath rock layers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'under' puts the treasure below the rock layers. 'Contains' looks like a container signal but just joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a scheme or ruse, the kind of secret scheme that a plot is.

clue.text: Creator of issue removed boxing article

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: far removed, distant
the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone who caused a problem is taken out of a boxing article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' means offspring here, not a problem or a magazine edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal word for children, and a father is a man who begets children.

clue.text: Album of new arrangement for strings?

blocks.note: first meaning: a recorded release of music
second meaning, whimsical: fitting cords again

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a string orchestration; the question mark admits the second reading splits the answer into a prefix meaning again and a word for a set of cords.
explanation.definitionFit: A recording is a captured musical performance issued as a disc, so an album is a recording.

clue.text: Rural pile has riding gear around yard

indicators.note: one word sits around the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for yard
tack is saddle, bridle and other horse equipment

explanation.surface: A country stable yard holds a heap of horse equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The word has wraps the yard abbreviation, then the riding gear follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A haystack is a large outdoor heap of hay, a pile found in the countryside.

clue.text: Absurdity of Nationalist version of "oneness"

indicators.note: a version is a different rendering, so the quoted word's letters are rewritten

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for Nationalist
its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A nationalist's idea of national unity is ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense is foolish talk or behaviour, something absurd or meaningless.

clue.text: Took another look at grey area lady uncovered

indicators.note: each word loses its covering, its outer letters, leaving the inside

blocks.note: the inner pair of letters
the inner pair of letters
the inner pair of letters

explanation.surface: Someone takes a second glance at a woman in a murky zone, perhaps exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: To reread a text is to read it again, taking a second look at it.

clue.text: Maniac chops yuppie's head off

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
off means awry or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter

explanation.surface: A madman decapitates a young professional, like the killer in American Psycho.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' reads as decapitation; in fact head picks a letter and off signals the reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A psycho is an informal word for a dangerously unstable person, a maniac.

clue.text: Conflict almost tore apart densely populated area

indicators.note: almost means not quite, so the final letter of the word is cut

blocks.note: war is armed conflict
to rend is to tear apart

explanation.surface: War nearly destroyed a crowded neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A warren is a network of rabbit burrows, and by extension a crowded maze of streets or buildings.

clue.text: Underground worker buries dead guard

indicators.note: burying something puts it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a miner works underground
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A miner buries a dead security guard.
explanation.walkthrough: A minder is British slang for a bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A minder is someone employed to protect another person, a bodyguard.

clue.text: Confines overambitious guards

indicators.note: the word guards something within itself, holding it inside

blocks.note: letters inside the word

explanation.surface: Restrictions keep an overreaching person in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confines' looks like a verb but is the noun, the bounds of something.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambit is the scope or bounds of something, its limits or confines.

clue.text: Britain managed to implicate one intelligence agent

indicators.note: to implicate is literally to fold in, so one piece is placed inside

blocks.note: B is an abbreviation for Britain
ran a business, managed it
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Britain manages to implicate a spy in some scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence agent' suggests a spy; it is the organ that does the thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain is the organ responsible for thought, the agent behind human intelligence.

clue.text: Line at end of letter lists retired fighters

indicators.note: retired means went back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a serif is the small stroke finishing a printed character
a ship that lists tips to one side

explanation.surface: A postscript tacked onto a letter names fighter pilots who have retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line at end of letter' suggests a P.S.; letter means a printed character. The Spitfire was the British fighter plane of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitfires were single-seat fighter aircraft flown by the RAF, now retired from service.

clue.text: Female insect without wings is centre of attention

indicators.note: wings are the sides, so the outer letters at both ends are removed

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
a swarming grasshopper

explanation.surface: A wingless female insect draws everyone's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: The focus is the central point on which attention or interest concentrates.

clue.text: Drunk actor in a rage, mainly rude and offensive when on the defensive

indicators.note: a drunk person is all over the place, so the letters are jumbled
mainly means most of, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before its tail is cut

explanation.surface: A drunken actor in a temper is rude and offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'offensive' in the surface is rudeness; in the definition it is a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard action is a defensive fight by retreating troops, an attack made while defending.

clue.text: She shouldn't have weed on monks shot by head of state

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or wrecked, so its letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters of the two words rearranged
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Monks are told off for smoking cannabis by a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Weed here is slang for tobacco, not cannabis or garden plants. ER is the Queen's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-smoker is a person who does not smoke tobacco, so she shouldn't be holding any.

clue.text: Good university dons get to continue without taking a break

indicators.note: to don is to put on, as one wears clothes, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
U is the abbreviation for university
to get a joke is to see it

explanation.surface: Good academics keep lecturing without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like university lecturers but is the verb, to put on, with the abbreviations wearing the understanding word around them.
explanation.definitionFit: To segue is to pass smoothly from one thing to the next without interruption.
